title: 08. GraphRAG: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval
summary: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval fuses two complementary retrieval signals: vector similarity (semantic closeness in embedding space) and graph traversal (structural relatedness via typed relationships).

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: **Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval** fuses two complementary retrieval signals: **vector similarity** (semantic closeness in embedding space) and **graph traversal** (structural relatedness via typed relationships). Vector search excels at finding conceptually similar entities even when they use different terminology — but it ignores relationship semantics ("invested in", "competed with"). Graph traversal follows precise typed relationships — but it misses entities not directly connected by edges. Combining both signals produces retrieval that is both semantically aware and structurally grounded. Key architectures: (1) **Sequential**: vector search → graph expansion; (2) **Parallel**: vector + graph simultaneously → score fusion; (3) **Graph-guided embedding**: train embeddings that encode graph structure (Node2Vec, TransE, GNNs). Production Graph RAG systems like Microsoft GraphRAG use the sequential approach; LightRAG uses a parallel dual-level approach.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
         HYBRID GRAPH-VECTOR RETRIEVAL ARCHITECTURE

  SEQUENTIAL (Retrieve-then-Expand)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                          │
  │  Query ──▶ [Embedder] ──▶ [Vector Index] ──▶ Top-K seeds│
  │                                                 │        │
  │                                                 ▼        │
  │                                   [Graph Expansion]      │
  │                                   BFS / PPR / Dijkstra   │
  │                                                 │        │
  │                                                 ▼        │
  │                                   Subgraph Context       │
  │                                   (entities + edges)     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  PARALLEL (Dual Retrieval + Fusion)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                          │
  │         ┌──[Vector Search]──▶ Top-K entities ──┐        │
  │  Query──┤                                       ├──▶[Fuse]│
  │         └──[Graph PPR/BFS]──▶ Top-K entities ──┘        │
  │                                                          │
  │  Fusion methods:                                         │
  │  • Linear: α*vec_score + (1-α)*graph_score              │
  │  • RRF: Σ 1/(60 + rank_i)                               │
  │  • Harmonic: 2*v*g/(v+g) — rewards both signals         │
  │  • Adaptive: α depends on detected query type           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  GRAPH EMBEDDING METHODS
  ┌─────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
  │ Method          │ Learns From    │ Use Case               │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ Node2Vec        │ Random walks   │ Structure similarity   │
  │ TransE          │ h+r≈t triples  │ Link prediction        │
  │ GraphSAGE       │ Neighbour agg  │ Inductive (new nodes)  │
  │ Sentence-BERT   │ Text only      │ Semantic similarity    │
  │ Fused (hybrid)  │ Text + walks   │ Best of both worlds    │
  └─────────────────┴────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

  SCORE CALIBRATION PROBLEM
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                          │
  │  Vector scores: 0.72  0.68  0.61  0.59  0.55  ...      │
  │  Graph scores:  0.008 0.003 0.002 0.001 0.0008 ...     │
  │                                                          │
  │  RAW fusion (α=0.5):                                     │
  │  Entity A: 0.5*0.72 + 0.5*0.008 = 0.364  ← vector wins │
  │                                                          │
  │  AFTER rank normalisation:                               │
  │  Vector rank: 1/5 → 0.2 → 0.5*0.2 = 0.10              │
  │  Graph rank:  1/5 → 0.2 → 0.5*0.2 = 0.10              │
  │  Combined: 0.20  ← fair balance                         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

quiz.explanation: Sequential (Retrieve-then-Expand): Vector search finds top-k semantically similar entities (seeds), then graph traversal expands to their k-hop neighbourhoods. quiz.explanation: TransE is a knowledge graph embedding model (2013) that represents entities and relations as vectors and optimises: for a valid triple (head, relation, tail), the embedding should satisfy h + r ≈ t (head + relation vector = tail vector). Training: minimise distance between (h + r) and t for positive triples; maximise distance for corrupted (negative) triples.

quiz.explanation: GraphSAGE (Graph Sample and Aggregate) is a Graph Neural Network (GNN) that learns a function to aggregate neighbourhood features into node embeddings. Unlike Node2Vec (transductive — only embeds seen nodes), GraphSAGE is inductive — it can embed unseen nodes by aggregating their neighbourhood features.

quiz.explanation: LightRAG implements a dual-level retrieval system: (1) Entity-level retrieval — vector search over entity embeddings to find relevant entities, then expand via graph; (2) Relationship-level retrieval — vector search over relationship embeddings (each relationship has its own embedding from its description/context).
